Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
818 PM EDT Mon Aug 31 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Earlier showers and thunderstorms have mostly weakened given
loss of diurnal heating.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Thunderstorm chances increase this week, but timing and 
  intensity remain uncertain.

- 2) Near-record early September heat expected.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Thunderstorm chances increase this week, but timing 
and intensity remain uncertain.

Any lingering showers dissipate this evening, with muggy and 
mostly cloudy skies tonight.

Looking at the rest of this week, the strong mid-level ridge 
positioned over the Mid-South will slowly push east toward the TN 
Valley. Numerous shortwave troughs / disturbances will round the top 
of the ridge, traversing the Great Lakes to Mid-Atlantic. This is 
going to bring us several rounds of thunderstorms, some of which 
could be strong to severe. The presence of strong lift and 
increasing shear, along with a hot and unstable airmass will produce 
an environment supporting of significant severe thunderstorms. The 
big caveat is timing. This setup can be very tricky to forecast 
exactly when these complexes of storms develop, and exactly where 
they track. The next shortwave is forecast to arrive Tuesday 
afternoon/evening. SPC has the northeast part of the forecast area 
in a Slight Risk (level 2 of 5), and a Marginal Risk (level 1 of 5) 
down into central VA. The latest 12Z guidance today has pushed back 
convection to Tuesday evening, and by that time we may avoid the 
worst of the severe weather impacts as storms arrive after peak 
daytime heating. 

SPC also has a Slight Risk across the area Wednesday through Friday 
as several additional shortwave troughs are expected to traverse the 
region. At some point this week, most likely toward the end when a 
strong upper trough digs south from Canada, we will be in a much 
more favorable position for the upper forcing, instability, and 
daytime heating to align. The latest AI/ML guidance indicates the 
highest chance for this is now on Thursday, but I would not discount 
any day for potentially strong to severe thunderstorms at this time. 

A cold front begins to slide south through the area Friday night 
into Saturday, bringing drier conditions and seasonal temperatures. 
Some thunderstorm chances linger south of I-66 on Saturday, then 
most of the area is dry and cooler come Sunday.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Near-record early September heat expected.

A strong ridge of high pressure over the southern Plains will 
build toward the Mid-South throughout this week. While humidity 
will be up to support several rounds of showers and thunderstorms, 
the heat will be up as well, especially Tuesday through Thursday.
High temperatures are expected to reach the lower to middle 90s 
Tuesday and Wednesday, while making a possible run at 100 degrees in 
a few spots in parts of eastern and northeastern Virginia, near the 
metros, and along the eastern areas of the Blue Ridge Mountains on 
Thursday. Heat indices, because of the humidity, will be high as 
well. Heat indices should reach 100 to 103 degrees in scattered 
places in interior parts of our region on Tuesday. Expect more 
widespread 100 to 105 degree heat indices on Wednesday. To round it 
off, Thursday will have heat indices readings more so in the 103 to 
105 degree ranges. These ranges can obviously change some by a few 
degrees warmer or a few degrees cooler. Either way, the point we 
want to make is it is going to be hot and humid through much of the 
week. Heat headlines could be issued soon regarding this 3-day 
stretch of heat and humidity. For the moment, monitor information at 
www.weather.gov. Even Friday, although may be cooler in terms of 
temperatures because of convection with a front, heat indices could 
still reach the 95 to 100 degree range in many places.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Some patchy fog or low clouds possible tonight, but not enough 
confidence to include in the TAFs. 

Looking at the rest of this week, while VFR conditions are expected 
to prevail there could be periods of sub-VFR conditions. Each 
morning, low clouds could develop due to a very moist environment, 
then lift by late morning as daytime heating strengthens. There will 
be complexes of thunderstorms moving across the region, but timing 
is uncertain. The next one could arrive Tuesday evening into Tuesday 
night, then several more rounds possible again sometime Wednesday 
through Friday. Conditions improve this weekend as cold front moves 
through the region.

&&

.MARINE...
Favorable marine conditions are expected through the week. 
Thunderstorm complexes are forecast to move from the Great Lakes to 
the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast at times this week. While the timing 
of exactly when this will occur remains uncertain, it is likely that 
Special Marine Warnings will be needed. Wind gusts in excess of 35-
40 knots and lightning strikes are going to be the main threats to 
mariners.

&&

.CLIMATE...
Near-record heat is possible, peaking Tuesday through Thursday.

Below is a list of record warm temperatures for September 1, 2, and 3.

(A '+' indicates the record also occurred in previous years).

The period of record for most sites dates back to the late 1800s,
